request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "My crew total" (`my-crew-due-total`). It adds up the due-totals of every crew led by the signed-in user's person. That person is found the same way "My due total" finds it, by name or alias, ignoring case. If the user has no person on the sheet, or their person leads no crew, the value is blank. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

I only changed the front end; no stored data, schema or server code was touched:
- **`core/session.ts`**: a new shared value holding each crew's lead and due-total.
- **`features/crews/crews.ts`**: the Crews section keeps that value up to date from the totals it already shows. This means the header total always matches the `crew-due-total` figures on screen.
- **`features/people/people.ts`**: the header picks out the crews the user's person leads, adds them up, and displays the result.
